summary: Jeffrey K. Riegel is a sinologist who taught Imre Galambos. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley (~1978–2007) and held a post at the University of Sydney (~2007–2017).

Jeffrey Kotyk works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa University (MA 2015–2016), under Terry Russell, and under James A. Benn at Leiden University (PhD 2017). He held posts at McMaster University and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey L. Broughton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1968–1975) and became a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (~1977).

Jeffrey Mehlman works in philosophy and other fields. He held academic posts at Cornell University (~1968–1974), Johns Hopkins University (~1974–1983), UC Berkeley (~1977–1978), Boston University (~1983), Harvard University, and Washington University in St. Louis.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University (~1964–1970) and held appointments at the University of Toronto (~1969–1980), UC Berkeley (Professor of Sanskrit, ~1977–1980), and the University of Michigan.
Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held posts as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (attested 2003) and at Berry College.

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under W. S. Karunatillake and earned his PhD under Karen C. Lang at the University of Virginia, later becoming Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University.

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (~1968–1972), Princeton University (~1972–1977), and the California Culinary Academy, later serving on the faculty at Princeton University (~1975–2018; Professor ~1986–2018).

Jeffrey Wayne Bass specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at UNC Wilmington (BA), University of Tennessee (MA), and UCLA (PhD under Gregory Schopen, also studying with James L. Fitzgerald and William M. Bodiford), he taught at UCLA and UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Shih completed an MA supervised by Geshe Lhundub Sopa and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisors Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has held professorships at the University of Oslo (2003) and the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (attested 2004), and taught Torkel Brekke and Lita Peipina.

Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1986–1999) and the University of Vienna, and became Professor and Managing Director of the Institute for Science of Religion at the University of Bern (~2006).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at LMU Munich (PhD), Göttingen (Habilitation), and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later holding professorships at Göttingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, Free University of Berlin, and LMU Munich.

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London in 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar in history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at the University of Oregon (~1965–1967) and Stanford University (~1968–1974), and held a post at Princeton University (~2001–2018).
Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He spent his career there (~1961–2008), serving as Professor from ~1983 to 2008.

Jessie Pons is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University (2011) and was appointed Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).
Ji Hao is a sinologist who completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota under the supervision of Paul Rouzer. He held an academic post at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).
Ji-yong Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts as professor (教授) at Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College (both attested 1976).

Jiang Wu is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nankai University and Harvard University (PhD 2002 under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello). He has served as a Professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
